title: Congressman joins fight to save Kips Bay AMC in New York City
shortDescription: New Yorkers are fighting to keep the Kips Bay AMC open after news broke that the theater would be closing its doors for good at the end of the year. Congressman Jerry Nadler joined other New York politicians in signing a letter to NYU Langone Health in hopes of saving the movie venue. Keith Powers, a NY assemblyman, previously said the health system now owns the land the AMC location sits on. "AMC Kip’s Bay has been one of Manhattan’s biggest and most cherished movie theaters since 1999," Nadler said in a post on X this week. "But the building has been sold to NYU Langone, and could permanently close at the end of this year." After hearing from constituents, Nadler said he decided to sign on to the letter. More than 8,400 people have signed the change.org petition entitled "Save the AMC Kips Bay 15 Theater from closure." As of now, no official closing date has been released. With the closure of AMC Kips Bay, there will be eight AMC locations left in Manhattan.
